**STEP 1 - Vessel type:** Flat square plate. It has a rim band and a flat centre with no inner wall or shadow.

**STEP 2 - Scale:** The plate spans about 340 px across. No reference object of known size is visible, so I used the square-plate range (20-30 cm) and took a typical 23 cm. Scale is about 340 / 23 ≈ 14.8 px/cm.

**STEP 3 - Food items:**
- **Melon/papaya cubes (orange):** About 10 cubes, roughly 2 cm each, in a patch of about 10 × 10 cm with gaps. Footprint about 45 cm². Average thickness about 1 cm. Volume about 45 cm³ × 0.6 g/ml ≈ 27 g, rounded to 40 g to allow for the cubes that are partly hidden.
- **Bacon:** Two cooked strips in a curled patch of about 10 × 9 cm. Footprint about 70 cm² × 0.8 ≈ 56 cm² of rough coverage. Thin, about 0.4 cm average. 56 × 0.4 × 1.0 ≈ 22 g, rounded to 25 g.
- **Roast potato cubes:** About 12 pieces of roughly 2 cm, in a patch of about 12 × 9 cm at around 50% coverage. Footprint about 48 cm². Average thickness about 1.2 cm. 48 × 1.2 × 1.0 ≈ 58 g, rounded to 60 g.

**STEP 4 - Hidden food:** No base layer or stacked food is visible. Items are a single layer, so no extra items are added.

**STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g (as served):** Melon about 34, bacon about 540 (cooked), roast potato about 150 (with some oil).

Total ≈ 125 g, about 240 kcal.
